Voat's FAQ currently says:

Submitting only links to sites you operate (or are associated with), without submitting other, unrelated links, is considered spamming. If you submit niche content (for example gaming videos from your own YouTube channel), you should create your own subverse and submit the content only to that subverse. If majority of the links you submit are to sites you are associated with, your domains may be globally banned from Voat. To be on the safe side, if you submit 10 links to various subverses on Voat, at most 2 of the 10 submitted links may be to the sites you are associated with.

While not a verbatim copy, it's more or less the same as reddit's self promotion rules

A search for "reddit self promotion" on YouTube shows lots of people who think they are bullshit.

So people draw images, make wallpapers, make poems, write essays, gather data, etc. and all of that is OK to post.
But if your hobby is making videos, it's all of a sudden sinful to show your work to other people?
Where's the logic in that?

(The part where the individual account is supposed to contribute 10 (or here at voat 5) times more than posting own stuff in that particular sub) goes contrary to common internet hygiene where people have multiple separate accounts for different activities and assumes that subs have completely isolated communities, which is obviously not true.

edit: it was pointed out by moe that the FAQ actually says "10 links to various subverses".

So tell me, why should self promotion be something that mods delete, instead of being voted on by the community like everything else?
Let's discuss the anti self promotion part of the FAQ that was copied over from Reddit

This post is very relevant to me, but I'll try to keep this short.

TL;DR: Let self-promotion happen site-wide. Let the community decide via reports and downvotes if it's spam or relevant to the subverse. Allow mods to ban domains in their sub to help stop spam of certain sites. Ideally, (and i understand this will take more work than just policy changes) we should be able to post a link to multiple subverses at once, and then the link is put on a time-out for a period of time before it can be posted again.

I'm one of the admins for a non-for-profit organization. The organization's primary focus is to try and share free information to help people be physically safe. Specifically, my site focuses on recreational substance users who may not have the best access to life-saving information. My website provides an open place for them to come ask questions and get non-judgemental answers, and none of us get paid any anything but good feels.

Ideally, I would like to be free to post about my site for two reasons: 1) I make no money off of this. In fact, i use my own personal money for some projects since we run on donations that help keep the servers going. So linking to my site gives me no personal gain but... 2) The site can seriously help people who need it. I'm 100% confident that we have saved multiple lives in the past. The more that drug-users have access to reliable information, the less chance they will do something risky and hurt themselves/others.

So far, I have kept my self-promotions to my voat. However, I feel it would be beneficial to others if the information I have was posted into other subs. I made a post in /v/drugs the other day, but i quickly deleted it since I was wondering OP's exact question. You can see from my comment history that although I'm a new Voat user, I enjoy the community and post about things other than my site. So on one hand I feel I should be free to distribute the information about my org.

On the other hand, as a moderator of a few subs on reddit, i recognize the spam problem. I can recognize that even though my information is helpful, that users don't want to see the same post in multiple verses at the same time. I don't want users hijacking my subverse for their own profit either. Perhaps a time limit can be set for how often a specific link can be posted? This would really limit the ability to repost to multiple subs, but i feel that's an entirely other issue and if multi-posting were an option, voat could make a timeout on links after they've been submitted. Perhaps this timeout would increase every time the link is posted and then reset after a certain period.

To help this, mods should be able to completely ban a domain from being submitted to their subverse. In the perfect word, we'd be able to have people who are regular contributors to the site be able to self-promote a bit, and they would be self-aware enough to not let it get super annoying. In the real world, people are probably going to be annoying, so i feel it should be left up to the individual subverses if self-promotion should be allowed.

I'm open to discuss any of the points I've made.

Some of the differences I can think of, off the top my head:

  1. The site is either based in Switzerland or Germany, so the legalities are very different from reddit.
  2. The codebase is completely new, in spite of the site being fuctionally very similiar.
  3. There is a limit to how many subs a user can moderate (10).
  4. Some RES-like features are built-in, such as expandos. Others are planned.
  5. Mods can set a minimum CCP (comment point) limit to downvoat in their subs. A recent rule change now excludes these subs from /v/all.
  6. Subs can enable an anonymous mode which replaces everyone's names with numbers. When enabled on the sub, it is not reversible. There is currently a bug that reveals the user's name in a reply notification, but I haven't confirmed it personally.
  7. Live point updates as well as notifications.
  8. AFAIK, self promotion is not completely banned and there is planned "partner" program. See the footer on every page.

That's all I can think of, but I'm sure there are more.
